_meta.note: patterns case guards the 14-log payload fix (was always-400 with 6) AND the bounded schema (3000 truncated). Re-locked 2026-08-24 (v2): tool rewritten front and back. The route was DOWN — callClaudeWithRetry already parses, so a second JSON.parse received "[object Object]" and threw on every call; MODELS.SONNET does not exist (SMART/FAST/DEEP); the helper takes two arguments, so label sat in a third that was ignored and maxTokens was camelCase against a snake_case option, leaving these schemas on the 2500 default. Adopted PF-39 v2 with a real guard profile (the rewrite declared outputGuard as a STRING, which reads as a declaration and enforces nothing) and runOutputGuard wired to both endpoints over every string field, with the visitor's own logs as the only source of truth. Frontend was English-only: 37 keys × 13 languages.

output.headline: Across 14 check-ins, stress and sleep scores moved together consistently: higher stress coincided with lower sleep and lower energy in every instance where stress reached 6 or above.

recurring_patterns.pattern: Stress 6+ coincides with energy 4 or below
recurring_patterns.evidence: Every check-in with stress rated 7 or higher (June 13, 17, 18 — 3 days) showed energy at 3 or below. No check-in with stress rated 3 or below had energy below 4.
recurring_patterns.limits: The logs do not show what drove stress on those days. Cause cannot be established from these entries alone.

recurring_patterns.pattern: Sleep 6 or below coincides with mood 5 or below
recurring_patterns.evidence: On days when sleep was rated 5 or below (June 13, 17, 18, 23), mood was consistently 4 or 5. On days when sleep was rated 6.5 or higher, mood ranged from 6 to 7. Days with sleep between 6 and 6.5 showed more variable mood.
recurring_patterns.limits: Sleep scores are self-reported and may reflect perceived rather than measured sleep. Direction of relationship cannot be determined from these logs.

recurring_patterns.pattern: A higher activity count appeared on some lower-energy days
recurring_patterns.evidence: On the two lowest-energy days in the log (June 18: energy 2, and June 13: energy 3), the activities recorded were 'deadline crunch' and 'back-to-back meetings' respectively. Both involved sustained high-demand work. This pattern appeared twice.
recurring_patterns.limits: Activity codes are not defined in the logs, so it is unknown what those activities represent or whether more activities caused, reflected, or were unrelated to the lower energy. Two observations is too few to call this a stable pattern.

day_or_week_patterns.observation: Low-point days appeared roughly mid-week in each of the two weeks logged
day_or_week_patterns.evidence: Energy and mood declined over several consecutive days twice in the log: June 10–13 and June 16–18. Both declines were followed by partial recovery. Two instances is too few to establish a recurring weekly cycle.

things_that_did_not_repeat: Physical signals: none logged on any day, so no pattern could form.
Caffeine and alcohol: both zero across all 14 days, so no variation to compare against.
Biometrics, weather, and menstrual cycle: not tracked in any entry.
The 21-activity count on June 13 was the single highest across all entries and did not recur at that level.

next_learning_step.track: Add a brief note on what the stress score reflects on any day rated 6 or above — for example, workload, a specific event, or physical discomfort.
next_learning_step.reason: Stress 6+ showed up alongside low energy and mood in every instance, but the logs give no information about what is driving the stress score. Even a few words per entry would let you see whether a specific type of stressor appears repeatedly, which would make the pattern more actionable.
